job_highlights.title: Responsibilities
items: The Operations Research Systems Analyst (ORSA) applies advanced quantitative methods, mathematical modeling, and systems analysis to optimize complex intelligence and operational processes across the Joint Intelligence Operations Center (JIOC)

Support operational planning teams with quantitative insights and structured analytical methodologies
Identify opportunities to improve processes, automate tasks, and enhance mission performance
Develop custom analytical tools, models, and approaches tailored to specific intelligence or operational requirements
Participate in JIOC intelligence planning conferences, exercises, J2 working groups, capability development sessions, national-level coordination boards, and technical exchange meetings

jobs_results.description:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We're a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies - collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation's health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose - and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

This is an opportunity for a motivated Operations Research Analyst to join MITRE's Operations Analysis department. We are a large group of over 60 operations research professionals, including over 20 PhDs, who provide thought leadership on a variety of strategic and technical issues, perform analysis that enable our sponsors to make more effective decisions, lead internal research and development activities to bring new technical capabilities into the public sector, and serve as trusted third-party advisors to government sponsors on a variety of technical topics. 

In short, we apply our problem-solving skills to complex interdisciplinary problems that occur within or at the intersection of organizations, operations, and technology.  We support sponsor projects across the defense and public sectors including homeland defense, military logistics, radio-spectrum frequency management, health care delivery, cybersecurity analytics, fraud detection, satellite planning, homeland security and civilian aviation. We apply advanced analytic techniques such as longitudinal analysis, large-scale integer programming, metaheuristics, agent-based modeling, reinforcement learning, predictive modeling, mathematical modeling, time series & forecasting, machine learning, optimization, statistics, probability modeling, regression analyses, Bayesian analysis, and different types of simulation to solve the nation's toughest problems. And our research pushes the boundaries on topics such as complex scheduling, medical image analysis, identifying changes in data streams and incorporating the latest AI advancements into our processes for efficiency and rigor.

If you are passionate about project-based analytical work in the public interest, you have found the right place.

Roles & Responsibilities:



Apply advanced analytical and mathematical modeling techniques to inform difficult policy and acquisition decisions, to maximize operational effectiveness and efficiency, and achieve highest quality engineering solutionsFrame problems, collect and manipulate data, develop & code customized algorithms, identify risks, and incorporate domain-specific context, as necessary & applicable, to supplement and enhance insight gained solely from mathematical analysesPresent results in an intuitive, actionable manner that can be understood by all sponsor audiences, regardless of technical expertise, including creative data visualization artifactsWork independently and collaborate with a team of technical staff and domain expertsWork successfully both in a remote environment and with in-person presence

Basic Qualifications:

 Typically requires less than 1 year of related experience with a related Bachelor's degree, or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.  Bachelor's degree in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Data Science/Analytics, Applied Mathematics/Statistics, or equivalent knowledge and skills in a related field  Be passionate about applying operations research, statistics, and data analytics to real world problems  Be willing to adapt and learn  Show evidence of knowledge of principles, concepts, methods and tools for conducting operations research, statistical analysis, and data analytic studies  Have experience in using tools and techniques to do mathematical modeling, optimization, statistics, probability modeling, and simulation  Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government's eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.  This position requires a minimum of 4 days a week on-site 

Preferred Qualifications:

 Demonstrated ability to use at least one optimization package (e.g., Gurobi, CPLEX, PuLP, AMPL)  Demonstrated ability to use at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, R, Java)  Demonstrated ability to use at least one simulation platform (e.g., Stella, Simio, Arena, AnyLogic, SimPy, RSimmer) Preference given to qualified candidates with active clearance (e.g. TS/SCI)Experience working with/for agencies and/or departments of the US Government (e.g., FAA, DoD, DoE, DHS, Treasury, IRS)Demonstrated ability to develop and incorporate a variety of AI/ML models, techniques, and principles into analytical work to efficiently achieve rigorous outcomes

jobs_results.description:
The Senior Operations Research Analyst / Team Lead provides advanced analytic support to a federal client while leading a small team of analysts. This role combines hands-on research, data fusion, geospatial and quantitative analysis with day-to-day technical leadership, work prioritization, quality assurance, mentorship, and delivery of analytically sound products.

How You Will Fulfill Your Mission Lead the delivery of analytical products that support operational planning, mission execution, and client decision-making by integrating research, data fusion, and advanced analytical methodologies. Guide the evaluation and interpretation of complex open-source, commercial, publicly available, and client-provided information to identify trends, relationships, risks, and mission-relevant insights.

Apply quantitative, qualitative, geospatial, and temporal analysis techniques to transform diverse datasets into actionable information for clients and stakeholders. Direct analytical activities across the team, establish priorities, allocate resources, and ensure deliverables meet quality, accuracy, and timeliness standards. Mentor and develop analysts through technical guidance, coaching, performance feedback, and collaborative problem-solving.

Partner with client representatives and internal leadership to define requirements, assess emerging needs, and address operational challenges affecting mission success. Produce and review reports, briefings, metrics, assessments, visualizations, and executive-level summaries that communicate analytical findings and program performance. Foster a culture of analytical rigor, accountability, and continuous improvement by maintaining sound tradecraft, quality control processes, and professional development within the team.

Why We Value You You are able to work independently and show a high level of initiative and attention to detail. You have a consistent character and do not yield to pressure to compromise or cut corners. You have a strong ability to communicate effectively with superiors, colleagues, and clients by clearly expressing your intent and understanding the focus and purpose of the conversation while allowing each person to get their point across.

You are open to new ideas and innovations and can create modifications or changes in yourself to adapt or suit a new environment/situation. You have faith in your own ideas and ability to be successful. You hold yourself to the highest standard and work to inspire your team to produce quality work.

Specific Knowledge/Certification Requirements Minimum Qualifications Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret clearance with eligibility for access to Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI). Demonstrated ability to lead and contribute within a team researching multifaceted problem sets in a dynamic environment. Demonstrated ability to work independently in research, data fusion, and analysis of multidisciplinary datasets. Ability to acquire, visualize, and analyze spatial and temporal data.

Strong critical-thinking and analytic tradecraft skills with the ability to deliver findings through written products, graphic annotation, briefings, or other client-directed formats. Experience working with commercial or publicly available datasets used in federal, defense, law-enforcement, or comparable analytic environments. Experience converting data from multiple sources into geospatial analysis and analytic products.

Experience with relevant analytic and geospatial tools such as Analyst's Notebook, ArcGIS Pro/ArcMap, Google Earth, or comparable platforms. Demonstrated experience providing technical direction, work prioritization, and quality oversight to other analysts.

Preferred Qualifications

Prior formal experience leading and mentoring an analytic team. Experience supporting complex federal, defense, law-enforcement, special operations, or comparable mission environments. Knowledge of structured analytic or targeting methodologies. Knowledge of multiple intelligence or information disciplines, including OSINT and related analytic sources. Experience with Publicly Available Information (PAI) and Commercially Available Information (CAI).

Working Conditions

The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions Physical Demands: While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be required to walk, sit, or stand for extended periods of time; reach with hands and arms; balance; stoop; talk or hear; have sufficient manual dexterity to operate a keyboard, calculator, telephone, and other such office equipment as necessary; may occasionally move and/or lift up to 50 pounds or more with assistance. Specific visual abilities required by the job include close vision, distant vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust and focus.

Work Environment:

Work will mainly be performed in an office setting and occasionally with irregular hours. The position may require access to client facilities, systems, data, or information Travel: A low amount of travel away from the office may be required.
